name: ClipVariations
listen_for: One bar of bass played five ways: as written, up a fourth, up a fifth and softer so the filter barely opens, then only its second half twice, an octave apart, all from one clip by placing it differently.

name: TempoRamp
listen_for: An arpeggio that speeds up smoothly to twice its tempo over two bars, then slows right down into its last note, because a tempo change can glide to the next one rather than jump.

name: AdditiveBell
listen_for: Struck inharmonic bell tones whose high partials die away first, leaving a low hum.

name: AudioRateAmplitudeModulation
listen_for: A buzzy line an octave below itself, because the signal's level is being wobbled at audio rate by a tone at half its pitch.

name: DrawbarOrgan
listen_for: An organ chord that starts round and hollow, then turns bright and full as upper drawbars are pulled out.

name: FrenchHorn
listen_for: A slow, round horn call that slides between legato notes, with a soft swell on each attack and no vibrato.

name: PhaseModElectricPiano
listen_for: A bell-edged electric piano whose attack gets brighter on harder notes, using phase modulation built from multiplied polynomials rather than a modulation input.

name: RingModulation
listen_for: Metallic, clangorous notes where the partials are sums and differences of two tones, not a scale of harmonics.

name: Subpatches
listen_for: A slow string chord made of three copies of one patch, a detuned pair of saws, at the note, an octave up and an octave down, each with its own width: a subpatch is written once and used as often as wanted.

name: Trumpet
listen_for: A bright fanfare whose notes scoop up to pitch and open out as they get louder, with vibrato arriving late on the long notes.

name: TwoOperatorFm
listen_for: A plucked FM bass: one sine bends the phase of another at the same pitch, by an amount that dies away in a fifth of a second and grows with velocity, so hard notes snap bright and soft ones stay round.

name: Clap
listen_for: A hand clap made of three quick noise bursts followed by a short tail, on the backbeat.

name: DrumLoop
listen_for: Kick, snare, clap and hats playing together as a two-bar loop.

name: HiHat
listen_for: An eighth-note hi-hat pattern of filtered noise with a longer open hat on the off-beat.

name: Kick808
listen_for: A deep kick drum whose pitch dives in the first few tens of milliseconds, then rings as a low tone.

name: RoundRobin
listen_for: A snare roll played twice: first from one recording, which buzzes like a machine gun, then taking three recordings in turn, so no two hits in a row are the same and it sounds played.

name: Snare
listen_for: A snare hit that mixes a short pitched body with a burst of band-limited noise.

name: AutoWah
listen_for: A funk clavinet through an envelope filter: the louder each note is played, the further a resonant filter opens and the more it quacks, as an insert follows its own input's level.

name: ChebyshevWavefold
listen_for: A sine that blooms through a vowel-like sweep of harmonics as its level rises into a fifth-order polynomial, then folds back to simple.

name: Chorus
listen_for: A clean chord made wider and gently wavering by two slowly moving delays; a faint grain on the top end is the delay stepping in whole samples.

name: Compressor
listen_for: A line of loud and soft notes evened out, with the hard hits held down so the quiet ones sit closer to them.

name: CubicSaturation
listen_for: The same note grows from clean to warmly distorted as velocity pushes it harder into a cubic curve.

name: Flanger
listen_for: A sustained buzzy tone with a jet-like sweep moving up and down through it.

name: HaasWidener
listen_for: A mono line that sounds wide because the right channel arrives twelve milliseconds later.

name: InsertFilterSweep
listen_for: A held chord whose filter opens over a second, automated on the insert through a stepped global parameter, the only route a clip has to an insert.

name: ParametricEq
listen_for: A held chord with one narrow 12 dB boost sweeping up through its harmonics, like a slow wah.

name: Phaser
listen_for: A held chord with soft notches sweeping slowly up and down its spectrum.

name: PingPongDelay
listen_for: Short notes whose echoes bounce left, right, left, right and fade away.

name: PrecutGrainCloud
listen_for: A shimmering cloud of overlapping tiny fragments of a tone, built from sixteen precut grains that the timeline triggers one by one.

name: Reverb
listen_for: Short plucks that bloom into a stereo room tail from a send bus of eight combs and four all-passes.

name: SidechainDucking
listen_for: A sustained pad that dips sharply on every kick and swells back, the classic pumping sound.

name: Vocoder
listen_for: A chord speaking a sequence of vowel shapes, with eight filter bands imposing a second track's formants on a saw.

name: ChipTune
listen_for: A chiptune in three channels, as an old console made it: a narrow pulse lead with vibrato, a triangle bass and noise drums, from naive oscillators and control-rate modulation, one voice a channel.

name: LeanDrumKit
listen_for: A drum kit at one voice a drum: a triangle kick whose pitch drops, a snare of a held sine and noise, and a hat that a new hit cuts off as a closed one does, with an open one now and then.

name: SmallRoom
listen_for: Struck chimes in a small room, a mono reverb of four short combs and two allpasses whose lines take 31 KB, half of what the board has, where the Reverb recipe's take 188 KB.

name: TapeEcho
listen_for: Plucked notes trailing echoes a dotted eighth apart, each one darker than the last, from a single comb whose line takes 36 KB: a feedback delay that fits the board.

name: FormantVowels
listen_for: A single sung note moving through ah, ee, oh and eh as three band-pass filters glide between vowel positions.

name: KeyboardTrackedFilter
listen_for: A rising arpeggio across five octaves that keeps the same tone colour because the cutoff follows the pitch.

name: ResonantSawBass
listen_for: A low saw line where each note opens with a resonant filter squelch that quickly closes.

name: VelocityFilterAmp
listen_for: One repeated note getting louder and brighter as it is struck harder, then falling back.

name: Wind
listen_for: A rising and falling whoosh of noise through a slowly wandering band-pass filter.

name: Arpeggio
listen_for: A steady up-and-down sixteenth-note arpeggio, written into the clip because the engine has no arpeggiator of its own.

name: AutoPan
listen_for: A chord that drifts smoothly from one ear to the other and back.

name: ChannelAftertouch
listen_for: A held chord that opens up as pressure rises and closes as it eases, modelled as one channel-wide parameter.

name: CurvedEnvelope
listen_for: Snappy plucks with a steep curved decay, made by multiplying an envelope by itself twice.

name: LegatoPortamento
listen_for: One unbroken monophonic line that slides between pitches with no new attack; the notes are a pitch ramp on a single held note.

name: LoopingEnvelope
listen_for: A held chord that retriggers its own decaying envelope every eighth note, using a looped sample of the envelope shape.

name: MacroKnob
listen_for: A dull, round note that a single macro turns bright, detuned and resonant while fading out its sub-octave.

name: MonoLead
listen_for: A single-voice lead where each new note cuts off the last and retriggers its filter and level envelopes.

name: PerVoiceLfo
listen_for: Three notes entering one by one that swell out of step, because each voice restarts its own LFO.

name: PitchBend
listen_for: A held note bent up a whole tone, down below where it started, then back to centre.

name: SampleAndHold
listen_for: A filter jumping to a new random cutoff eight times a second, using a looped stepped sample as the random source.

name: SawLfoFilter
listen_for: A filter that repeatedly climbs and then snaps back three times a second, using a saw oscillator as a per-note LFO.

name: SharedLfo
listen_for: Three notes entering one by one that all swell together, because one LFO runs for the whole track.

name: SquareLfoFilter
listen_for: A filter jumping between dark and bright three times a second, using a square oscillator as a per-note LFO.

name: StepSequencer
listen_for: An eight-step acid-like bass loop repeating four times, with each step setting its own pitch and filter cutoff.

name: TempoSyncedLfo
listen_for: A filter wobbling exactly twice per beat at 120 beats per minute, with the rate worked out by hand for this tempo.

name: TranceGate
listen_for: A held chord chopped into sharp sixteenth notes at 120 beats per minute by a low-frequency square wave.

name: Tremolo
listen_for: Sustained notes pulsing smoothly in volume six times a second.

name: TriangleLfoFilter
listen_for: A filter sweep that rises and falls in straight lines three times a second, using a triangle oscillator as a per-note LFO.

name: VibratoModWheel
listen_for: A held note that starts straight, then gains a singing vibrato as the mod wheel rises.

name: VoiceStealing
listen_for: A three-note pattern of long notes on two voices, where each new note cuts the oldest off abruptly with a faint tick.

name: DetunedSupersaw
listen_for: A wide, shimmering chord stack where seven detuned saws beat slowly against each other on every note.

name: HardSync
listen_for: A tearing lead whose every note starts as a bright, vocal rasp and settles into a plain saw, because a second oscillator restarts with each cycle of the first while its own pitch falls back toward it.

name: LoopedSample
listen_for: A sustained chord that holds as long as the notes are down because each sample loops, then fades on release.

name: OneShotSample
listen_for: One recorded hit replayed at seven pitches, ringing to its own end even though each key is released at once.

name: PluckedString
listen_for: A Karplus-Strong guitar-like line where each noise burst rings as a pitched string and darkens as it fades.

name: PwmPad
listen_for: A slow chord pad whose tone hollows and thickens as the pulse width sweeps.

name: ReleaseSamples
listen_for: A plucked keyboard whose every key coming up adds a soft wooden thunk, a recording the sampler plays only when a note is let go, whether it is short or held.

name: ReverseSwell
listen_for: A cymbal sucked in backwards, swelling into a low boom where the same recording then crashes forwards, because a sampler can play a recording from its end to its start.

name: StereoUnison
listen_for: One wide lead note spread across the stereo field, with five detuned saws panned from left to right.

name: SubOscillator
listen_for: A saw line with a square wave one octave below that adds weight under each note.

name: VelocityLayers
listen_for: The same note struck softly and hard, flipping to a brighter recording above the middle of the velocity range.

name: WavetableMorph
listen_for: Two long notes that each sweep smoothly from a pure sine, through a hollow square-like wave, to a bright saw, using three looped single-cycle samples.
